paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between co-occurrence number and accuracy (ACC %) for various editing methods on BioMedLM. The x-axis represents the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 1 to 10^4, with regularly spaced tick labels. The y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %) on a linear scale, ranging from 40% to 65%, with regularly spaced tick labels at 5% intervals. The plot features six lines, each representing a different method: Base (black, circle markers, solid line), FT (blue, triangle markers, solid line), IKE (red, triangle markers, solid line), MEND (brown, square markers, solid line), MEMIT (purple, diamond markers, solid line), and ROME (green, square markers, solid line). The Base line starts at approximately 40% and increases steadily to around 44%. The FT line begins at approximately 42% and rises to about 48%. The IKE line starts at around 44% and increases to approximately 52%. The MEND line begins at approximately 45% and rises to around 56%. The MEMIT line starts at approximately 46% and increases to about 55%. The ROME line begins at approximately 51% and rises steadily to around 66%.
